title: Minimum Number of Groups to Create a Valid Assignment
summary: Given a set of numbered balls, determine the minimum number of boxes needed for sorting, ensuring that balls with the same number can be in different boxes, and the difference in the number of balls between the largest and smallest boxes does not exceed one.
statement: Given a set of numbered balls, determine the minimum number of boxes needed for sorting, ensuring that balls with the same number can be in different boxes, and the difference in the number of balls between the largest and smallest boxes does not exceed one.
constraints: Partition equal values into groups; a group cannot mix values.
Across all groups, sizes may differ by at most one; minimize the group count.
hints: For a chosen smaller size k, every group has size k or k+1.
Try k downward from the minimum frequency and test whether each frequency can be split into those sizes.
Feasibility is count//k >= count%k; add ceil(count/(k+1)).
The first feasible largest k creates the fewest groups, and the inequality exactly measures whether remainders can be distributed.
editorial: The first feasible largest k creates the fewest groups, and the inequality exactly measures whether remainders can be distributed.
